Hamdori

# A hamster lives in the corner of your desktop

A lifelike hamster lives in a borderless, see-through window on your desktop. It loves a gentle rub, gathers seeds while you type, and takes breaks with you.

Adopt for $3.99Launch price · $4.99 from December 1

 Pay once, no subscription
 Up to 3 computers
 Apple silicon Mac · Windows 10/11

Hi! Want to work together?

## Next to you all day

Every clip below shows the real app.

### Pet it

Rub it gently with your cursor and it closes its eyes and sends up hearts.

 

### Pick it up

Press and drag the hamster and it dangles along. Set it down and it sometimes shakes itself off.

 

### Toys to play with [...] See the steps

1. Open the Hamdori installer you downloaded.
2. When "Windows protected your PC" appears, click "More info".
3. The publisher shows as "Unknown publisher". If you downloaded the file from this site, click "Run anyway".
4. When setup finishes, Hamdori appears in the corner of your screen. Enter the key from your receipt.

On Windows 11 PCs with Smart App Control turned on, the installer may be blocked. You won't have activated your key yet, so you can get a refund. Download the installer only from this site.

## And while you work

### Take breaks together

Right-click the hamster, choose Break Together, then click the little clock. Focus for 25 minutes, then rest for 5 together.

 

### Points out big unused apps [...] ### Points out big unused apps

When memory runs low, it shows memory-heavy apps you're not using. Only an app you pick and confirm is asked to quit, the same way you'd quit it yourself.

 

### File drawer

Drop files on the hamster to keep them in its drawer. Drag a row onto another app to use the file. The original stays where it is.

## Safe to keep around

 

  No monitoring permissionsIt works without Accessibility, Screen Recording or Input Monitoring access. It asks about notifications only if you turn them on.
 

  It never sees what you typeOn a Mac it reads only how many keys were pressed; on Windows, only the time of the last keyboard or mouse input. For the mouse, only how many clicks, scrolls and moves, and where the cursor is. Never which key.

@galdayanThanks for asking! On macOS I use CGEventSourceCounterForEventType(kCGEventSourceStateHIDSystemState, kCGEventKeyDown). It returns a count of key-down events, with no key codes, characters or app names. Hamdori checks it every 0.1 seconds, and when the count goes up, he nibbles.

The app never asks for Input Monitoring, and in my testing this call works without any permission prompt.

On Windows I use GetLastInputInfo, which only gives the time of the last input, not a key-press count.
